newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Afternoon Update.

text.p: LEADERS MEET BEFORE PREMIER'S CONFERENCE
State and Territory leaders are meeting in Canberra ahead of tomorrow's Premiers Confernce.
The Premiers and Chief Ministers are holding preliminary talks on a number of key issues including native title and future federal funding to the states and territories.
The meeting comes ahead of a dinner tonight with the Prime Minister at The Lodge, during which they'll discuss ways of responding to the High Court's contentious Wik judgement.
OPPOSITION PROBES POLICE INVOLVEMENT IN COLSTON COSTS
The Federal Opposition has asked about police involvement in the investigation into Independent Senator Mal Colston's use of travel allowances.

Opposition Senate Leader, John Faulkner, has asked Senate President, Margaret Reid, if Australian Federal Police have visited the Senate Department regarding the investigation into Senator Colston's use of travel allowances.
Senator Colston's use of travel allowance is subject to two Departmental inquiries, but he's consistently denied any wrong-doing.
Senator Faulkner asked if police inquired about the methodology of the inquiry and expressed concern about the investigative process.
He also asked if police had requested to see the reports on Senator Colston, and if that request was granted.
Senator Reid said she has no information on any police inquiries and will pursue the issue.
VICTORIAN MAN SERIOUSLY WOUNDED IN POLICE SHOOTING
In Melbourne, a man has been seriously wounded during the second shooting by Victoria Police officers this month.
The 20-year-old has been taken to the nearby Western hospital with chest wounds after he was shot in Footscray shortly after two o'clock this afternoon.
Police say a number of shots were fired outside a medical clinic, after officers pursued a man, who was wearing a wig and looked suspicious.
Earlier this month, a 27-year-old man died after he was shot following an armed robbery on a pharmacy at Thomastown, in Melbourne's north.
BANKS CREATE ATM NETWORK
Westpac says there is little chance of all banks linking automatic teller machines despite three of Australia's four big banks agreeing to create a combined network.
ANZ, Westpac and National Australia Bank will have a ATM network of about 5,500 machines.
Westpac's Rob Bishop says the more advanced features of ATMs, such as providing mini-statements, will only be able to be used by a bank's customers.
Customers will still be charged a fee for using another bank's ATM, despite the network agreement.
SOLDIER KILLED AT TANDEM THRUST
The Defence Department says the soldier killed in an accident during Exercise Tandem Thrust this morning was 26-year-old Brendan Casey, of Wyong in New South Wales.
The Department says Captain Casey, a member of the First Battalion Royal Australian Regiment in Townsville, was injured at about 1.30am.
He died three hours after the accident, which happened at the Shoalwater Bay Training Area.
The United States and Australian Commanders of Tandem Thrust, Vice Admiral, Robert Natter, and Major General Tim Ford have expressed sympathy to Captain Casey's family.
They say safety has been a top priority in the exercise and the accident has left them very sad.
STILL HOPE FOR CREW OF WRECKED YACHT
An Australian Maritime Safety Authority official says there is still hope for the crew of a yacht, missing in rough conditions in the Coral Sea, after lifejackets and debris were found today.
Bits of wood and what's believed to be submerged sails were found a short time ago, near where the emergency beacons and lifejackets were found.
David Gray says searchers are hoping to find a life-raft this afternoon in the region of the wreckage.
Mr Gray says the movement of Cyclone Justin is making it hard for rescue coordinators to work out wind patterns.
Two Queenslanders, an 18-year-old girl and a 53-year-old man, and three New Zealand men were on board the yacht when it sent a distress signal from near the eye of Cyclone Justin on Tuesday.
TOP MURDER DETECTIVE BROUGHT IN ON SERIAL CASE

One of Western Australia's most experienced detectives has been brought in to oversee the investigation into the disappearance of Perth women, Ciarra Glennon and Sarah Spiers, and the murder of Jane Rimmer.
Superintendent Dick Lane has joined the macro enquiry team with a specific role to monitor the strategic direction of the inquiry.
Superintendent Lane is one of the state's top murder detectives and was previously in charge of the major crime squad.
Acting Superintendent, Paul Ferguson, will continue as manager of the Macro Task Force.
